question: Can an LLM's own in-context use of rich environment feedback (runtime errors, judge text, or sibling successes) be turned into dense token-level credit assignment for RL, without an external teacher?
hypothesis: A policy conditioned on feedback (a self-teacher) is more accurate than the unconditioned student, so distilling its next-token predictions into the student gives better credit assignment than scalar-reward GRPO; gains should grow with the base model's in-context learning ability.
contributions: Formalise Reinforcement Learning with Rich Feedback (RLRF), where environments return tokenized feedback beyond a scalar reward

Introduce Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO), an on-policy algorithm that distills the feedback-conditioned self-teacher into the policy; a policy-gradient method with advantages swapped for log-ratio of teacher to student
Show gains over GRPO in science QA, tool use and LiveCodeBench v6, shorter reasoning, and 3x faster discovery on hard questions via test-time self-distillation

method.summary: SDPO samples G rollouts per question from the current policy, gets environment feedback (or uses a successful sibling rollout as feedback), re-scores the original rollout under the same model reprompted with that feedback (the self-teacher), and minimises a stop-gradient top-K logit-level divergence between student and teacher. Compared with an improved GRPO on Qwen3-8B and Olmo3-7B-Instruct.
method.task: RL post-training with verifiable rewards and rich feedback (science QA, tool use, competitive programming); test-time training on single hard questions

training.objective: L_SDPO = sum_t KL(pi_theta(.|x,y<t) || stopgrad(pi_theta(.|x,f,y<t))), approximated with top-K plus tail term; equivalent to policy gradient with advantage A_{i,t}(y)=log pi(y|x,f_i,y<t)/pi(y|x,y<t). Sections 3 uses Jensen-Shannon, Sections 4-5 reverse-KL.
training.lr: 1e-5 constant (Section 3); 1e-6 constant (Sections 4 and 5). GRPO: 1e-6 default / 1e-5 on-policy
training.batch_size: question batch 32 (Sec 3, 4), 1 (Sec 5 TTT); rollouts per question 8 (Sec 3, 4), 16 (Sec 5); mini batch 32 (Sec 3, on-policy), 1 (Sec 4 and 5 columns per Table 12 layout)
training.steps: LCBv6 curves to step 80-90; Section 3 budgeted by wall clock (1h and 5h)
training.regularisation: gradient clip norm 1.0; teacher EMA update rate 0.05 (Sec 3) / 0.01 (Sec 4, 5); rollout importance sampling clip 2; advantage clip 5.0 (TTT); top-K distillation K=100 (Sec 3), 20 (Sec 4, 5)
training.hardware: single node, 4x NVIDIA GH200 (378GB VRAM); PyTorch container 25.02-py3, CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.7.0, verl, FSDP2, vLLM
training.compute: each Section 3 run approximately 6 hours including initialization and validation
training.wall_clock: ~6 h per Section 3 run; SDPO step +5.8% (no code env) / +17.1% (with code env) over GRPO per Fig 5

other.hyperparameter_search_section3: GRPO grid lr {1e-5,1e-6} x minibatch {8,32}; on-policy GRPO same lr, minibatch 32; SDPO grid over KL variant (forward KL, JS), lr, minibatch; one config per method chosen on 5h validation accuracy across all datasets and models

limits: Depends on the model's in-context learning ability: primarily applicable to stronger base models and can underperform GRPO on weaker models (Qwen2.5-1.5B)
Depends on quality of environment feedback; uninformative or misleading feedback may not help
Small compute overhead for log-probs of the teacher, may matter for small models with short generations
Only tested with at most 8B models, on-policy updates only (off-policy variant left to future work), single node, no agentic or long-horizon tasks
Hyperparameters in Section 3 selected on validation accuracy at 5h, same data used to report test numbers in Table 3 (validation/test split not detailed)
Section 3 train/test split sizes and the number of SciKnowEval and ToolAlpaca items are not given
SDPO advantages are biased with respect to expected reward (Section 4.5)
